Music.Models.ace-step.xl-turbo.Pros:
Pros
• Follows style and request details well.
• Emotional vocals.
• Many settings and recipes.
Music.Models.ace-step.xl-turbo.Cons:
Cons
• Demanding VRAM use; powerful GPUs with 24 GB are the target.
• Complex arrangements with 3+ vocal roles have not yet been confirmed as stable.
Music.Models.ace-step.xl-turbo.Memory:
Memory use
Tested on an RTX 4090 with 24 GB VRAM and a PC with 128 GB RAM.
In repeated j-pop generations with automatic duration, 8 steps and the LM enabled, the ACE process used up to 19.1 GB VRAM and 14.2 GB resident RAM.
These are model-process readings, excluding the interface and other applications; other requests and durations may use different amounts of memory.

Music.Expert.Description.cfg_scale: Automatic uses the model default. Manual 1 uses one branch; other values need two and increase memory use. Strong guidance can damage audio.
Music.Expert.Description.cot: Full planning includes chords. Melody planning uses melody only. With no plan the model creates a sequence directly: results are less predictable and automatic guidance needs two processing branches.
Music.Expert.Description.lm_seed: Automatic picks a new number. A fixed number helps repeat the plan. Each variant increments it by 1. Repeating a finished track uses its saved numbers and settings.
Music.Expert.Description.max_tokens: Maximum generated elements. Larger values leave less room for lyrics and need more memory. Sequence generation is also capped by duration: 25 elements per second.
Music.Expert.Description.min_tokens: The usual end signal is blocked until this many elements are generated. Must not exceed the maximum. Sequence size is capped by requested duration (25 elements per second).
Music.Expert.Description.peak_clip: Clipped peak samples per million allowed during normalization (0–999). Higher is louder but can distort. Recommended: 10.
Music.Expert.Description.penalty_window: Number of recent elements considered for repetition control. From 1 to 100.
Music.Expert.Description.repetition_pena: 1 disables control; above 1 discourages repeats; below 1 encourages them. Excessive control can disrupt rhythm and structure.
Music.Expert.Description.seed: Automatic produces a new sound variant. A fixed number helps repeat results, but does not guarantee identical output on other hardware. Each variant increments it by 1.
Music.Expert.Description.steps: Number of sound rendering steps. More takes longer; improvement is not guaranteed. Recommended: 32.
Music.Expert.Description.temperature: Lower values make choices more predictable; higher values add surprises, including errors and noise. 0 is the strictest choice.
Music.Expert.Description.top_k: How many of the most likely candidates are considered. Fewer means stricter; more means greater variety.
Music.Expert.Description.top_p: Total probability covered by allowed candidates. Lower values narrow the choice. From 0.001 to 1.

About.Guide.Start: Choose model and result folders, check your computer passport and select Start. The standard downloader verifies hardware libraries separately from models, including after a hardware change. It shows size and preparation progress; downloads can be resumed. Scenario entry checks its components. Model weights are not bundled in the installer. Internet access is needed for downloads, updates and network tools. Check again in the literary scenario performs full file verification.
About.Guide.Images: Add an image or a group, choose an available mode suitable for your PC, configure the description, and start analysis. Review the result and use the available saving, export or speech options. Choose standard prompts or create your own; in custom mode, your prompt text replaces some regular description settings.
About.Guide.Literary: Create a project or continue a saved one. Your manuscript is on the left and the assistants are on the right. Transfer the Writer output into the editor manually. Copy all on a reply copies only that message. Expand the chapter panel at the lower-right edge of the editor for chapter operations and export. Watch the save indicator.
About.Guide.SendingTitle: Sending to the Advisor and Writer
About.Guide.Sending: The blue button sends to the Advisor and returns to that role from the Writer. The red button hands work to the Writer; availability depends on the action and any required explanation. The role label only identifies the current assistant. Right-click the role or either send button for project settings. Defaults: Enter sends to the Advisor, Ctrl+Enter to the Writer, and Shift+Enter adds a newline. The first two shortcuts are configurable. Direct request prepares the brief privately and starts the Writer immediately. With it disabled, the brief is shown before further work. Discuss revisions with the Advisor. Sending clears the input and shows an activity indicator; Stop interrupts the request.
About.Guide.Sources: Select the context sources you need: concept, anchors, completed parts, RAG, Jelly memory, and the future route. The RAG editor separates the original source from the current project. Saving updates the index; changes to chapters require memory review. The pencil at the bottom-right of the Route panel opens stage editing and creation. A future plan is not already-written text.
About.Guide.Memory: Review proposed facts, edit fields, or uncheck a record to exclude it. Invalid fields are highlighted in red. A quotation must match a continuous passage in the source; a paraphrase is not a quotation. Editing a fact does not change the manuscript. A structurally valid record does not guarantee semantic accuracy: you make the final decision.
About.Guide.Prompts: In the literary workspace, the top-bar pencil opens standard or custom prompt set selection and library management. Standard texts are built into the application; you can edit your own copies. Prompts appear vertically in collapsible groups and subcategories. The editor provides search, undo/redo, line wrapping, and standard text. Plot anchors have a separate top-bar button.
About.Guide.Updates: Open updates here or in Settings. Stable searches for a full installer; Beta searches for file updates in the shared version stream. Read accumulated changes and download size, download, then choose Update now or At next launch. Closing the window does not authorize installation. Automatic checks mark an available version, with a green dot in the tray. Save important work before updating.

About.Author: Author — PiTrolKun

About.Intro: LOPATA is a local AI workshop for Windows: image analysis and generation, literary work, file processing and screen capture. Finance and Sandbox are experiments. Choose a task, prepare its components and review the result.
About.Choice: Start by configuring model and result folders, reviewing your PC profile, and choosing a workflow. Models are downloaded separately after you review their licenses. Requirements and speed depend on your hardware and the selected mode.
About.Control: The application is released as a test Beta. Sandbox remains experimental. Models can make mistakes; descriptions of future capabilities do not mean those features are already implemented.
About.Why: Local AI can already do a lot, but getting started often means searching for suitable applications, models and instructions. LOPATA grew from a desire to shorten that journey for people with home and gaming PCs. Instead of assembling a separate set of applications for every task, the aim is a shared environment that makes it clear where to start, what is needed and where the result will be saved.
About.Tasks: Analysis describes images; literary work combines a manuscript, Advisor, Writer and memory. Generation creates images from prompts. Utilities process files and capture the screen; the finance experiment helps discuss expenses and income.
About.Hardware: Main GGUF scenarios and image generation use separate CPU/Vulkan bundles. Giga, Jelly and SwinIR use managed PyTorch CPU/CUDA/XPU/supported Windows ROCm profiles. Selection depends on working operations, driver and available memory. A proven GPU hardware failure permits one safe CPU retry; partially displayed answers are not silently repeated. CPU and RTX 4090 have been tested; physical AMD/Intel GPUs have not. Kimi uses the CPU/RAM profile. Drivers are not installed automatically.
About.Local: The main work should run on your own computer where possible. The internet remains useful for downloads, updates and tasks that need outside information. The idea is to rely on your own computer and deliberately choose when external resources are needed, rather than to avoid the internet entirely.
About.TrustTitle: AI assistance still needs human judgement
About.Trust: A model can make mistakes and is not treated as all-powerful. The project’s design calls for understandable access to files, the network and computer actions, limited to the work at hand. Important actions and downloads should remain under user control. You can review, refine and save an answer; the final decision about using it stays with you.
About.Future: AI evolves quickly, so LOPATA should not depend on one particular model. The tools inside the application can change while the familiar path from a task to a result remains. This guides development: improve capabilities gradually without making people start learning everything again.
About.Open: LOPATA is a personal open-source project, a hobby and a practical experiment with AI, including AI-assisted development. Ideas are discussed, checked and tested in real use. Documentation keeps decisions, limitations and unsuccessful attempts so that someone else can understand why things work as they do, fix what is needed and continue even without the original author.
About.Status: Public versions and release notes are available in the repository releases. The version of this running copy is shown at the top of this window. A development version may differ from the published beta. See the user guide for current instructions and the project documentation for the decision history.

About.Guide.Navigation: After Start work, choose Creation, Analysis, Experiments or Processing / utilities. The feature map helps find a scenario by a familiar term or function. Cards open the entrance to the corresponding section.
About.Guide.Generation: Creation → Images → Simple generation. Prepare Z-Image Turbo or Krea 2 Turbo. ИИ± in the header switches installed models; the adjacent ⌫ clears the workspace while keeping saved files. Enter sends a prompt; Shift+Enter inserts a line break. Sent text immediately enters the chat and can be selected and copied. ✨ improves entered text or creates a random prompt when empty, without sending; Ctrl+Z undoes the insertion. 📎 uses the Beta image analyzer to extract the whole scene, background, characters or style as editable text. If Beta is missing, a separate preparation window installs it; click 📎 again afterwards. Controls below the input select aspect ratio, generation size, variant count and another result from the same prompt. ▦⤢ selects the saved output size: original, 720p, 1080p or 4K, preserving proportions without AI reconstruction. Results are automatically saved to the configured folder; right-click an image for actions. Metadata includes the prompt, model and parameters; author is the profile name or LOPATA User.
About.Guide.ImageUtility: Processing / utilities → Images → Image processing. Add files, a folder, links (one per line), or clipboard contents; the generation folder opens in the standard file picker. Drag sources from the left folder tree; right-click to open a file or Explorer. Choose a method in a separate window: seven built-in methods and three downloadable AI tools. The favorite is the default. Select a 360p–8K preset, format, output folder and naming mode; Convert format only preserves dimensions. Presets set the longest side and preserve proportions. Settings have explanations; AI can change details. Originals stay unchanged and results are separate; multiple files get a batch folder. Icons beside the list start, pause/resume, stop, retry failures, remove selected entries and clear the list. Removing an entry does not delete its source. Duplicates are marked red; failures get three retries. Drag dividers to resize panels; progress and the log appear on the right.
About.Guide.Shell: Right-click an image → LOPATA → To WebP or Enlarge ×2. These commands replace the selected original: the new file is created and checked before replacing or deleting the source. Use the utility to keep originals. Commands run without showing the window; if LOPATA is closed, it starts in the background and remains in the tray. Integration is enabled by default; disable it in Settings → General → Windows integration. Menu placement depends on Explorer; Windows may require Show more options.
About.Guide.Capture: Processing / utilities → Screen capture. Choose a screenshot, GIF or video and the capture area. Utility settings provide the output folder, recording options and hotkeys. Stop recording when finished; files are saved locally. Check the capture area and screen contents before recording.
About.Guide.Finance: Experiments → Personal finance → Monthly expense calculation. Choose a model, currency and survey period; enter recurring expenses and income. For partial external coverage, enter your own share; full external coverage means zero personal expense. Changing currency changes the label without converting amounts. Local calculations, reports and AI discussion are available after the survey. Review model suggestions yourself.
About.Guide.Background: The gear opens searchable settings. General controls the close button, Windows startup and automatic continuation. Hiding in the tray preserves the page and does not stop work; an explicit pause is separate. The tray menu returns to work and controls the available background operation. Connected operations save checkpoints; automatic continuation waits 60 seconds after startup. A green dot means an update; red means an unread result from a long task. Helper windows close independently; recovery depends on the scenario.

About.Guide.Music: Prepare components, enter lyrics or select instrumental mode, then choose your preferences. Stress accents and markers remain editable text; their accuracy requires practical testing. Title, variants and desired duration are on the right. The red button starts or pauses generation; the cross cancels it. Results are saved in the selected folder and appear in the player. Opus at 320 kbps is the default; MP3, FLAC and WAV are also available. The + control adds one file of the same audio in another format and becomes − to remove the additional copy. Artist and title are separate inputs; empty placeholders are never exported. The subtle Comment input at the top is stored in tags. Files also carry lyrics, Style, both resolved seeds, parameters, model and generation provenance. Two formats share one card; format buttons choose the file to play, while copy transfers both files. Existing WAV files remain usable. Repeat uses the saved request. Pausing unfinished synthesis restarts that stage; completed plans and tracks are retained. Poetry chat and rhyme improvement are not available yet. Available memory is checked on entry and before stages. Main settings show graphics card or processor and the CPU fallback reason. GPU paths include CUDA SM86/89/120 and compatible Vulkan devices; only RTX4090 has been physically tested. A GPU initialization or allocation failure retries the unfinished stage once on CPU with the same inputs. The gear at the bottom of the right panel opens expert settings: plain-language labels, technical names on hover, descriptions and recommended defaults. User presets can be saved, updated, renamed, deleted, imported and exported as JSON. Apply saves model settings; each job keeps its own snapshot for repeat generation. No-plan mode skips the ABC stage. Stronger guidance needs more memory. The poetry chat placeholder is on the left of the same bottom toolbar. The Composition and performance circle controls related parameters; prompt influence is adjusted separately. Manual values are pinned in expert settings and retained when the circle moves. The book icon beside the gear opens recipes with full descriptions, exact parameters and sources. Browsing and canceling do not change settings; Apply is explicit. Simple and expert presets are stored separately. The prompt influence explanation is available through the question-mark button. Circle positions for arbitrary expert values may be approximate; the numbers are retained. Open projects using the folder icon at the bottom of the text toolbar. A temporary project is saved after its first request or a manual save. Т/⚙/○ switches between lyrics history, settings history and disabled arrows. Intermediate edits are not recorded; new requests append to history. The project window shows errors and cancellations. Finish or cancel a job, including a paused job, before switching projects. On the YuE2 Q8 entrance, listen to our example and Suno. Icons save the MP3 files and open parameters in a separate window. Reuse settings transfers the local lyrics and settings without generation; the output folder and history are kept.

Music.Models.Description.yue2: Song generator using lyrics and music wishes.
Music.Models.yue2.q8.Pros:
Pros
• Many settings to shape the result.
• In successful takes, sound and music quality is close to cloud results in our tests.
Music.Models.yue2.q8.Memory:
Memory
• Estimated headroom for a song up to 6 minutes with about 1,000 input tokens: 8 GB of free VRAM; with stronger task guidance, 13 GB.
• For CPU execution instead of GPU: 12–17 GB of free RAM and AVX2 support.
Usage depends on text length, duration, planning mode and settings. These are estimates with headroom, not measured peaks. LOPATA checks available memory before starting.
Music.Models.yue2.q8.Cons:
Cons
• May take liberties with lyrics, tags and music wishes.
• Results depend heavily on settings.
• The chance of getting the desired result on the first run is low: several attempts and setting adjustments are often needed.
Music.Models.Description.ace-step: ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo · official music and song generation pipeline. Separate language, BPM, meter and key fields; auxiliary 1.7B LM. Expert settings are connected. Quality and memory use await testing; circle mapping is not enabled.
Music.Models.Description.diffrhythm:
DiffRhythm 2 is a lightweight local model for quickly creating songs from lyrics, with a focus on structure, preserving words, and Chinese/English vocals. Suitable for quick batches of generations and style experiments;
Russian is not officially supported: the model preserves most words but sings them with pronounced Chinese phonetics and an accent; attentive listening generally preserves the meaning. This can be useful as the effect of a foreign performer.
Music.Models.Description.heartmula: Independent candidate for testing lyrics and style control, Russian, genres and memory use.
Music.Models.Description.songgeneration: Research candidate for testing lyric accuracy. Limitations, resources and integration terms remain to be confirmed.
Music.Models.Description.minimax: Roadmap candidate for songs from descriptions and lyrics. Areas of interest include long Russian lyrics and the rate of successful takes.
Music.Models.Description.regrind: ACE-Step community branch. Planned evaluation covers natural vocals and result consistency.
Music.Models.Description.mothersuperior: YuE2 research branches involving real audio and sound adaptation. A research direction, not a connected package.
Music.Models.Description.yue2-lora: Joint adaptation of YuE2 composition and performance. Compatibility, language and style effects require testing.
Music.Models.Description.mulacover: Specialized cover and remix direction using reference audio or melodies. Does not replace the main lyrics-to-song workflow.
Music.Models.Description.yingmusic: Candidate for controlled vocals from words and melody. A possible part of a future song creation and mixing pipeline.
Music.Models.Description.vibe: Candidate for background and instrumental music. The roadmap does not present it as the main generator of songs with specified lyrics.
Music.Models.Description.midasheng: Later direction for music, speech, effects and ambience. A possible component of a mixed audio pipeline.
Music.Models.yue2.bf16.Description: YuE2 3B BF16 · original Safetensors and official Python inference. Generator and VAE download separately. Its own passport. Sample genres differ: punk for BF16, doom metal for Suno.
Music.Models.yue2.bf16.Pros:
Pros
• In our tests, Russian lyric adherence is easier to achieve and broken words and pronunciation are quicker to improve.
• Original precision without quantization.
• Many settings, a circle and separate presets; defaults use the selected successful sample settings.
Music.Models.yue2.bf16.Cons:
Cons
• In our tests, randomness is comparable to Q8: even successful settings may produce missing or reordered lines.
• Significantly slower generation: early RTX 4090 runs took about 7–14 minutes versus roughly 2 minutes with quantized Q8. This is a reference, not a comparison with identical settings.
• Uses a single seed; Q8 peak_clip is unsupported.
Music.Models.yue2.bf16.Memory:
Memory
• For comfortable use, we recommend an RTX 5090 or a comparable, more powerful compatible GPU. This is a recommendation, not a minimum requirement.
• First RTX 4090 test: 18.4 GB VRAM on the reported peak screenshot versus 2.6 GB idle, an increase of about 15.8 GB.
• System RAM: 45 GB during generation versus 38 GB idle, an increase of about 7 GB. Process memory was not measured separately. This is one test observation, not minimum requirements.
• Developer reference: 24 GB VRAM and 24 GiB free RAM. LOPATA checks memory and estimates reserves from the request and CFG before running.
• AR and VAE move between GPU and RAM across stages without quantization. Other devices and requests need separate measurements.
Music.Expert.TransferConfirm: This preset belongs to another YuE2 variation. Transfer compatible settings only? Unsupported parameters and circle positions are not transferred; the original preset remains unchanged.
Music.Models.yue2.bf16.RecipeWarning: Defaults use the selected successful BF16 sample settings. Other recipes are adapted to shared parameters; Q8 results do not establish their effectiveness here. Complete lyrics and repeatability are not guaranteed.
Cloud.Description.music_studio: Separate Studio server using existing Q8 weights, its own settings and passport, and a shared project. Practical quality comparison.
Music.Models.yue2.studio-q8.Description: A fast, stable local model with good adherence to genre, lyrics and vocal descriptions. Strong with solo vocals and duets. Its main weakness is inconsistent separation of three or more vocal roles; performance can sometimes be less emotive than cloud models.
Music.Models.yue2.studio-q8.Pros:
Pros
• Good adherence to the requested genre and vocal character.
• Good results with Russian lyrics, solo vocals and duets.
• Many settings: bubble control, expert parameters and presets.
Music.Models.yue2.studio-q8.Cons:
Cons
• With three or more vocal roles, it may mix performers and their parts.
• Sometimes less expressive and emotive than cloud models.
Music.Models.yue2.studio-q8.Memory:
Memory usage
In our RTX 4090 test: up to 5.8 GiB VRAM and 3.4 GiB RAM while generating a complete song. Studio processes only, excluding other applications.
Music.Ace.Hint.bpm: 0 = automatic; otherwise 30–300 beats per minute. Slow/fast wishes remain in caption.
Music.Ace.Hint.vocal_language: auto follows a single performer language. Multiple languages remain unknown.
Music.Ace.Hint.timesignature: auto follows wishes. 2, 3, 4, 6 are supported meters; empty lets the model estimate.
Music.Ace.Hint.keyscale: For example C major or F# minor. Empty = automatic.
Music.Ace.Hint.seed: −1 = new random attempt. Otherwise an integer; variants run sequentially.
Music.Ace.Hint.inference_steps: 1 to 20; Turbo defaults to 8. Legacy values above 20 are clamped to 20 at launch and logged. Custom timesteps have priority. More steps do not guarantee better results.
Music.Ace.Hint.shift: Diffusion step distribution. Explicit timesteps replace shift and step count.
Music.Ace.Hint.infer_method: Official ode and sde modes; does not change model family.
Music.Ace.Hint.sampler_mode: euler or heun. Uses the official ACE sampler.
Music.Ace.Hint.velocity_norm_threshold: 0 = disabled. Bounds latent changes during diffusion.
Music.Ace.Hint.timesteps: Empty uses the default. Descending numbers in 0…1, comma-separated: 1,0.8,0.5,0.2,0.
Music.Ace.Hint.thinking: LM creates audio codes before diffusion. CoT can run separately with thinking off.
Music.Ace.Hint.use_cot_metas: LM fills missing BPM, meter, key and duration. Explicit values have priority.
Music.Ace.Hint.use_cot_caption: Allow LM to refine the sound caption. Original and effective requests are saved.
Music.Ace.Hint.use_cot_language: LM detects a language when not specified. Lyrics are not rewritten.
Music.Ace.Hint.use_constrained_decoding: Official LM musical metadata format constraints.
Music.Ace.Hint.lm_temperature: LM sampling randomness. Applies only when LM is used.
Music.Ace.Hint.lm_cfg_scale: Auxiliary LM CFG. This is separate from Turbo diffusion guidance.
Music.Ace.Hint.lm_negative_prompt: Empty follows Avoid wishes. Applies to LM with CFG > 1; caption restrictions remain.
Music.Ace.Hint.dcw_enabled: Auto follows Turbo defaults; Off disables; On enables.
Music.Ace.Hint.dcw_mode: Official ACE modes: low, high, double, pix.
Music.Ace.Hint.dcw_scaler: Wavelet correction coefficient; applies with DCW enabled.
Music.Ace.Hint.normalization_db: Target peak in dB; applies when normalization is enabled.
Music.Ace.Hint.latent_shift: Official latent offset before audio decoding.
Music.Ace.Hint.retake_variance: 0 = ordinary generation; higher values mix noise with retake_seed.
Music.Ace.Hint.offload_to_cpu: Auto follows ACE VRAM policy. Offload reduces VRAM use and can slow execution.
Music.Ace.Hint.offload_dit_to_cpu: Auto follows ACE policy. Separate from other component offload.
Music.Ace.Hint.lm_offload_to_cpu: Auto follows memory policy; separately controls the auxiliary LM.
Music.Ace.Hint.use_flash_attention: This Windows bundle does not include flash-attn. Uses official SDPA/eager attention.
Music.Ace.Hint.compile_model: torch.compile needs a compatible compiler. First launch can take much longer; disabled by default.
Music.Ace.Hint.constrained_decoding_debu: Constrained decoding diagnostics. Does not improve quality by itself.
Music.Ace.ExpertHint: ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo · official Python API. Separate presets; circle mapping is not enabled. Lyrics are not rewritten. Variants, duration and format are in the main window.
Music.Ace.Unsupported: Unavailable for XL Turbo: diffusion CFG, ADG and CFG interval (Base parameters). Cover/repaint, LoRA and training are future stages. No quantization; original weights are used.
Music.Ace.NoTransfer: ACE and YuE settings are incompatible. Select a preset for the same model.
Music.Ace.EditorHint: ACE: encoder limits are 2048 lyric tokens and 256 caption/metadata tokens. The official tokenizer checks exact input before conditioning; excess input raises an error instead of silent truncation.
Music.DiffRhythm.ExpertHint: Author DiffRhythm 2 parameters. Set duration in main settings: up to 240 seconds; Automatic means 240 seconds. Russian frontend is experimental. Audio reference and instrumental mode are not connected yet.
Music.DiffRhythm.Hint.seed: −1 chooses a new random seed for each variant; an integer fixes initial randomness.
Music.DiffRhythm.Hint.steps: Default 16. More steps increase computation; quality improvement is not guaranteed.
Music.DiffRhythm.Hint.cfg: Author DiffRhythm CFG. Default 1.3; independent of the YuE and ACE circles.
Music.DiffRhythm.Hint.fake_stereo: 1 uses author delayed pseudo-stereo; 0 produces mono. Channels are not generated independently.
Music.DiffRhythm.Hint.experimental_ru: 1 uses eSpeak RU with explicit phoneme mapping to the trained vocabulary. Listening quality is unverified. 0 uses author English/Chinese; Cyrillic causes an explicit error.
